observations: ClickHouse documents a GitHub-events dataset sourced from GH Archive and exposes it through a public SQL playground; the dataset is maintained for interactive queries and includes PushEvent/repository/time fields.

ClickHouse also states that the dataset is a structured copy of GH Archive and, as of 2026, recent GH Archive coverage is dominated by PushEvent records, making the class relevant to commit-push corroboration.

A no-login public query path is documented, but the current scheduled-Chat web surface could not submit the required arbitrary SQL POST and therefore did not directly observe the target SHA in the third-party index during this bounded slice.

The direct-query route depends on externally hosted ClickHouse query compute. Under the current Phase-1 zero-dependency contract, that hosted-compute dependency cannot count as an accepted scheduled-Chat-native mechanism even if the public demo is free and anonymous.

ClickHouse advertises a downloadable redistribution of the dataset, but this bounded slice did not establish a target-SHA-addressable static lookup that avoids hosted query compute; downloading/scanning the full multi-billion-record dataset is not a direct exact-object retrieval mechanism on the current scheduled-Chat surface.
